headline: Too Many Thoughts (Instrumental)
description:
"Too Many Thoughts" is an AI-generated music exploration of what goes on in my head when there's too much. Too many to-dos, too much pressure, no idea where to start. The whole thing just freezes. What helps me is leaving. Walking. Being outside. Slowly the thoughts sort themselves at their own pace, and at some point it gets quiet again. From there I can actually begin.
The track follows that arc in sound: starts fragmented and dense, ends somewhere close to stillness.
workflow:
The track was built in Suno using the two-field system. Style field for the sonic world, Lyrics field for the arc through four structure tags.
It took around six generations to get it right. The glitchy fragmented opening was the hardest moment to land. Most versions were either too chaotic with no direction or too clean too early. The one that worked had a genuine tension in it, the glitches feeling like actual fragmented thoughts rather than decoration, and the piano motif emerging from the noise slowly enough that the break into clarity actually meant something.
That moment, when the chaos drops and the solo piano arrives, is the emotional center of the whole track. Everything before it is weight. The piano is the release.
prompt: Modern instrumental, neoclassical electronic, cinematic. Opens chaotic and fragmented, glitchy granular textures, overlapping synth arpeggios out of phase, scattered piano shards, anxious low pulse like a racing heart. A repeating motif slowly emerges from the noise. Tension builds, then breaks into clarity, a single introspective solo piano line, warm reverb, spacious, melancholic but hopeful. 75 bpm. In the spirit of Nils Frahm, Jon Hopkins, Ólafur Arnalds.
structure:
[Intro: chaotic, glitchy, fragmented thoughts]
[Build: tension, repeating motif emerging]
[Break: clarity arrives]
[Outro: solo piano, resolution]
reflection: First experiment with Suno. The structural tags worked surprisingly well for an instrumental. Suno actually followed the arc from chaos to clarity. The glitchy textures in the intro feel almost too fitting for the theme, like the AI understood what overthinking sounds like. The piano break lands with real weight. Rough around the edges, but that roughness carries the meaning.

workflow: The vocal version was created using Suno's Cover feature directly from the instrumental track. The same sonic world, same arc, same structure but with vocals and lyrics added on top. Suno generated the lyrics automatically and I made adjustments to get them closer to the actual feeling. Starting from the existing track meant the voice had to find its way into something already built rather than the music being shaped around the lyrics from the beginning. That tension between the fragmented glitchy texture underneath and the words on top is what makes this version feel different from a track that was written as a song from the start.

headline: Open Water (Hybrid)
description:
Open Water is about what happens when nature is bigger than you and you stop fighting that.
The wind doesn't ask. The water doesn't wait. You step into it and suddenly your body has to be completely present. The cold hits your skin. The force pulls at you. You feel every muscle, every breath, every heartbeat.
Out there you remember what it feels like to be alive in a body. Not thinking. Not planning. Just feeling the weight of the water, the pull of the wind, the ground under your feet. Every sense switched on at once.
That is the feeling this track is chasing. The size of the ocean. The force of the wind. The strange fullness of being completely, physically here.
workflow:
The base track was generated in Suno with a driving hybrid electronic style, female vocals, and the full lyrics structure. Suno gave the song its arc and vocal performance but the production felt too polished and generic.
To get more depth and raw energy, the Suno track was uploaded into Stable Audio's audio-to-audio feature. Using the same sonic concept as a prompt, 808 sub-bass, four-on-the-floor kick, wind textures, Berlin techno drive, Stable Audio rebuilt the production layer while preserving the structure. The result is heavier, more physical, and closer to the actual feeling of standing at the ocean than the Suno version alone.
The two tools do different things well.
Suno handles vocals and song structure. Stable Audio handles texture, depth, and raw sonic power. Chaining them together gets you closer to both.
prompt: modern neoclassical electronic cinematic hybrid organic electronic driving and euphoric wind textures oceanic space swelling pads pulsing mid tempo build powerful and free female vocals soaring melodic delivery warm analog production 95 bpm in the spirit of nils frahm jon hopkins electronic, downtempo, trip hop, chillout, ambient
structure:
[Intro: wide open, wind texture, distant horizon, electronic pulse begins]
[Build: energy rises, swelling pads, the kite catches wind, momentum]
[Chorus: euphoric release, soaring vocals, full sound, power and freedom]
[Verse 2: grounded again, present in the body, salt air, movement]
[Build: bigger this time, unstoppable]
[Final Chorus: everything open, no ceiling, pure liberation]
[Outro: the wind carries it out, fades to space]

headline: Night Run
description:
Night Run is what happens when the day finally lets go.
The city is still moving but the noise has changed. It is darker, looser, more alive in a different way. You are out, running, and your mind starts running on its own. No pressure. No direction. Just ideas arriving, one after the other, like the city is feeding them to you.
This track lives in that state. Dark and hypnotic, something underneath it always pushing forward. The beats don't stop but they breathe. There is space in it, and in that space something creative opens up.
workflow:
Night Run was generated directly in Stable Audio, no Suno involved. For a fully instrumental dark electronic track Stable Audio is the stronger tool. It handles hypnotic texture, layered beats, and experimental sound design better than Suno without vocals in the mix.
The prompt focused on three building blocks: dark experimental IDM as the genre, 120 BPM, and a mood of electric and mysterious. On top of that, specific rhythm components were named explicitly, deep kick drum, metallic hi-hats, glitchy stuttering percussion, because Stable Audio needs rhythm described in detail to actually deliver beats rather than atmosphere alone.
Two to three generations were compared and the strongest version selected based on how well the hypnotic loop quality held across the full track length.
prompt: Dark hypnotic experimental electronic instrumental, perfect for a late night city walk where ideas start flowing, titled "Night Run". Featuring a deep pounding kick drum, hypnotic layered synth loops that shift and evolve, glitchy stuttering percussion, dark sub-bass with long decay, metallic hi-hats with irregular rhythm, and unexpected textural breaks that open up space. The mood is alive, mysterious, unpredictable, and electric. 120 BPM, relentless but hypnotic. Berlin underground techno meets experimental IDM, late night analog warmth, raw and layered production.
